prior_art.basis: Independent review by claude-independent-prior-art-reviewer-20261106: No open or discoverable enzyme digests any plastic in hours; fast enzymatic depolymerisation is solved only for PET and some polyesters, so the Main KPI of 100,000,000 tonnes of plastic digested per year is unmet. For PET, Carbios's engineered cutinase depolymerised 90% of PET waste in 10 hours (Nature 2020), and its plant was planned for over 130 tonnes per day (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carbios); FAST-PETase is openly published (709 citations, https://europepmc.org/article/MED/35478237). For the plastics that dominate production the answer is missing: a review finds research has mostly not produced working biocatalysts for polyethylene, polypropylene, PVC, polystyrene, ether-based polyurethane, polyamide and synthetic rubber (https://europepmc.org/article/MED/36099200), nylon-6 enzymes are only at screening stage (https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-45523-5), and claims of insect polystyrene digestion are disputed (https://doi.org/10.1039/d5su00725a). Open discovery resources exist (PlaszymeDB, PETadex and metagenomic miners on GitHub) but list candidates, not hours-scale polyolefin enzymes. Honest limit: PET hydrolase engineering is a known answer, so tasks that re-engineer PETases or replicate LCC-ICCG or FAST-PETase are not new work; the open, checkable work is a verified enzyme or enzyme-plus-pretreatment route for polyolefins, PVC or polystyrene.
